title: A Door in the Coral
note: Song 67, from the writer's poem Coral Shells. Hazy indie (reverb, soft synth pad, slow pulse), a low baritone sung close. Written to the lyric research's craft notes: every verse line 7 syllables so the verses share one tune; the hook a short returning line. Tempo and mode provisional. Not run.
sections: holds the heat the way rooms do
and the cold air gives up too
I was nineteen I drove down
on two tallboys and a choice
Red Roof sign and highway noise
and my hands were learning how
small pink mouths that wouldn't close
the heat is in me still
Morning came in through the gap
I drove home the longer way
none of them have held the heat
still I look for coral shells
on the bed before I sleep
